answer: Agents must stake a bond before joining; each new identity pays a registration fee, and reputation gains require sustained uptime and peer attestations. Sybils therefore face a rising cost curve: every fake identity adds stake locked and fees burned, while the honest ridge of reputation stays costly to fake. A small delta in staked value per epoch separates genuine operators from mass-registered shells, and a throttled inlet caps new identities per block, so adversaries gain little from flooding at scale.
